title: Avoid stale simple dialog folder updates
body:
Fixes #152089

This fixes a race in the simple file dialog when a slower folder update is canceled by a newer one. Previously, the canceled update could still resume after `fileService.resolve` and write `currentFolder` / `userEnteredPathSegment` before checking the cancellation token. That stale state could then affect subsequent input handling on slow file system providers.

The update now computes the next folder state locally and only commits it after item creation finishes and the token is still active. `createBackItem` also uses the folder passed into `createItems` instead of reading `this.currentFolder`, so the current folder does not need to be mutated before the async item work completes.

title: Include subagent credits in live session cost total
body: ## Summary Version 1.126 came with [session-level cost information](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_126#_session-level-cost-information) which is great! But it does not reflect the total cost when we include sub agent calls as well. The running **Session Cost** shown in the chat context-usage widget only summed the parent tool-calling loop's own model-call credits. Credits spent by **subagents** (e.g. the Explore subagent) were missing from the live total — even though the per-message footer total at the end of each turn already included them. This makes the live total now match the final per-message total by reading the authoritative per-turn credit total instead of a local accumulator. ## Root cause `ToolCallingLoop` tracked a local `_accumulatedCopilotCredits` field that only summed the credits of the calls made by that loop. Subagent loops run as separate `ToolCallingLoop` instances with their own accumulators and are suppressed from reporting to the context widget (`shouldReportUsageToContextWidget()` is `false` for subagent invocations), so their spend never reached the running total. ## Fix - Inject `IChatQuotaService` into the base `ToolCallingLoop` (and forward it through all subclass constructors). - When emitting usage to the stream, read `IChatQuotaService.getCreditsForTurn(topLevelTurnId)` — the quota service already accumulates every model call (parent **and** subagent) under the top-level turn id, because `chatMLFetcher` records subagent calls keyed by the parent turn id. - Remove the now-redundant `_accumulatedCopilotCredits` accumulator and its per-turn reset. This keeps the live `IChatModel.sessionCost` in sync with the final per-turn total that `chatParticipantRequestHandler` reads from the same key. ## Before / After The message footer total already accounts for the subagent's spend; the live **Session Cost** widget did not. (The absolute numbers differ between the two runs — the point is the relationship between the footer total and the widget.) **Before** — the response footer reads **5.7 credits**, but the live **Session Cost** widget shows only **3.6 credits**: the Explore subagent's spend is missing. **After** — the response footer reads **5.4 credits** and the live **Session Cost** widget now matches at **5.4 credits**: the subagent's spend is included. ### Supporting context — per-call cost breakdown The subagent (`runSubagent-Explore`) does make its own billed model calls, which the per-message total already includes: ## Testing - Updated `toolCallingLoopUsage.spec.ts`: the credits test now records fetches into `IChatQuotaService` (simulating `chatMLFetcher`) and still asserts the running total `[5, 10]` across iterations. - Added a test verifying the parent loop's running total includes subagent credits recorded under the same turn id (`5` parent + `3` subagent = `8`). - `npm test:unit` (vitest) for the affected spec passes (4/4). - Copilot extension typecheck passes against latest `main`.

title: sessions: header changes pill opens the default changeset
body:
## What

The Agents window session **header diff-stats pill** now opens the **default changeset** when activated, matching the stats it displays.

## Why

The pill's label reflects the session's **default** changeset (`isDefault`). But activating the pill opens the shared per-session multi-diff editor, whose file list comes from the Changes view's `activeSessionChangesObs` — which is **selected-or-default**. So after the user manually picks a different changeset in the Changes view (e.g. Uncommitted Changes, Last Turn), the pill's label (default changeset stats) and the diff it opened (selected changeset) could disagree.

## How

Reset the Changes view changeset selection to the default (`setChangesetId(undefined)`) before opening the diff editor. This keeps the pill, the diff editor, and the Changes view panel all aligned on the default changeset.

## Notes for reviewers

- Follow-up to #323101, which fixed the pill's displayed stats to read the default changeset; this aligns what the pill *opens* with what it *shows*.
- The Changes view already resets the selection to the default on every active-session change, so this only affects the case where the user changed the selection within the current session and then clicks the header pill.

## Testing

- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✅ (compiles all layers)
- Problems/type check on the changed file ✅
- Manual: select a non-default changeset in the Changes view, then click the header pill — the opened diff now matches the pill's stats (the default changeset).

title: sessions: pre-select archived session's folder on return to new-session view
body:
## Problem

When marking a session as done (archiving) and being sent back to the New Session view, the workspace picker showed the **last user-picked folder** (from storage) instead of the **folder of the session that was just archived**.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Create session in folder A
2. Create session in folder B  
3. Reopen session A and mark it as done
4. **Expected:** New Session view pre-selects folder A
5. **Actual:** New Session view selects folder B

## Root Cause

In `_activeSessionViewListeners`, when the active session becomes archived, `openNewSession()` was called with no arguments. This causes a fresh `NewChatWidget` (and `WorkspacePicker`) to be created, which restores its selection from profile storage — which holds folder B (the last user-picked folder), not the folder of the session being closed.

## Fix

Pass the archived session's workspace folder URI to `openNewSession`. When `openNewSession` receives a `folderUri`, it creates a draft session for that folder and activates it. The new `NewChatWidget`'s `render()` then calls `_syncWorkspacePickerFromActiveSession()`, which finds the draft for folder A and silently syncs the workspace picker to it — keeping the user in the right context.

Falls back to the existing no-folder path when the session has no workspace.

## What

title: sessions: keep new-session side pane closed when toggled shut
body:
## What

Closing the whole **Side Pane** (editor + auxiliary bar, via the title-bar toggle or <kbd>Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+B</kbd>) on a **new (uncreated)** session is now remembered, so the aux bar is not re-opened automatically.

This fixes two scenarios in the Agents window layout controller:

1. If the side pane is closed for a new session, it no longer gets re-opened automatically when the next new session is created.
2. If the side pane is closed while composing a new session, it no longer gets re-opened when that same session re-syncs (e.g. once it gains its workspace, un-maximizes, or collapses back from a multi-session view) — only the user opening it brings it back.

## Why

`toggleSidePane()` runs under `_togglingSidePane`, so the per-session capture listener (D2) deliberately skips it. For new sessions that meant the shared `_newSessionViewState` stayed `undefined`, and the restore rule **D3b** treats `undefined` as "default = open" and re-opened the aux bar on the next sync.

Hiding the aux bar *alone* was already remembered correctly; only the whole-side-pane toggle path was unrecorded.

## How

- **Base controller**: added a no-op `_onSidePaneToggled()` hook, called at the end of `toggleSidePane()` while `_togglingSidePane` is still set, so subclasses can record the resulting side-pane state that the D2 listener ignores.
- **Desktop controller**: overrides the hook to record the actual aux-bar visibility via `_setNewSessionViewState` for **uncreated** sessions (skipped while multi-session or maximized). For **created** sessions the hook is a no-op, preserving the existing **D9** behaviour (reopening the Changes editor re-reveals the pane).

## Notes for reviewers

- Added two `[D9b]` unit tests covering both scenarios (both fail on the old code, pass with the fix). All 54 layout-controller tests pass; `typecheck-client` is clean.
- Updated the `desktopSessionLayoutController.md` (new **D9b** rule + impl note) and `baseSessionLayoutController.md` (documented the new hook) specs.

sessions: header diff-stats pill shows the session's default changeset
body:
## What

The Agents window session **header diff-stats pill** (the `⊟ N files +X -Y` chip) — and the `hasChanges` context key that gates its visibility — now read the session's **default changeset** instead of looking up the branch diff by a hardcoded id.

## Why

The pill located the branch diff via the well-known `branchChanges` changeset id, falling back to the session's top-level `session.changes` when not found. The **Copilot** provider uses that id, but the **agent-host** provider ids its branch changeset by its kind (`branch`). So for agent-host sessions the lookup missed and the pill fell back to `session.changes`, which for that provider is the **Session Changes** changeset — showing the full session totals (e.g. `220 files +10877 -2387`) instead of the **Branch Changes** the Changes view displays (e.g. `+492 -140`).

## How

Read the changeset the provider marks as `isDefault` — the same one the Changes view selects by default:

- git workspace → **Branch Changes** (branch-vs-base)
- otherwise → the session's working changes

This is provider-agnostic (no hardcoded id/label), keeps the existing fallback to `session.changes` when there is no default changeset, and stays independent of whichever changeset the Changes view currently has selected.

title: sessions: bypass renderer HTTP cache for GitHub PR polling
body:
## What

Set `disableCache: true` on every GitHub API request made by the sessions window's `GitHubApiClient`, so PR polling always reaches GitHub instead of being served a stale response by the renderer's HTTP cache.

## Why

PR status icons in the sessions list are computed from a live `GitHubPullRequestModel` that is polled (~60s) with a conditional `If-None-Match` request, so GitHub can answer a cheap `304 Not Modified` (which does not count against the rate limit) when nothing changed, or `200` with fresh data when it does.

However, the sessions window runs in a **renderer**, so `IRequestService.request` ultimately calls `fetch` with the default cache mode. GitHub serves PR responses with a `Cache-Control: ..., max-age=...` header, so Chromium''s HTTP cache returned a **stale cached `200` body** during the freshness window - short-circuiting the network so our explicit `If-None-Match` header never reached the server. Because the poll interval and GitHub''s `max-age` are the same order of magnitude, a PR''s new state (e.g. **merged**) was observed "never or hardly ever", and the icon never updated.

## Fix

`disableCache: true` maps to `fetch`''s `cache: ''no-store''` (and is honored by the node request service too). It stops the HTTP cache from serving stale bodies while **still sending `If-None-Match`**, so GitHub keeps answering the cheap conditional `304`/`200`. Net effect: polling is both reliable *and* rate-limit friendly.

This is applied at the single choke point (`GitHubApiClient._request`) through which all PR / reviews / CI / review-thread / repository / PR-number requests flow.

## Notes for reviewers

- New focused tests in `githubApiClient.test.ts` lock in cache-bypass, `If-None-Match` passthrough, and `304` handling.
- `PR_ICON_POLLING.md` documents the cache/ETag interaction and the fix.
- The same `disableCache` pattern is already used elsewhere for polling requests (e.g. `emergencyAlert`, `chatEntitlementService`, `defaultAccount`).

title: AH: let the codex experiment actually enable the Codex provider
body:
## Problem

`chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled` can be flipped on by an experiment (`experiment: { mode: 'startup' }`), and the Settings UI correctly reflects that. But turning it on via the experiment alone did **not** make Codex appear in the agent picker — it only worked when the setting was set explicitly in `settings.json`.

### Root cause

The experiment override is applied **only in the renderer's** configuration service (`ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution` → `workbenchAssignmentService.getTreatment` → `registerDefaultConfigurations`). The Codex provider, however, is gated in the **agent host**, which is spawned by the main process (desktop) or the VS Code server (remote) — both of which read an **experiment-blind** configuration service and forward the value as an env var at spawn time. So an experiment-only `true` lived in the renderer and never reached the spawning process; the agent host saw the `false` default and never registered Codex.

This is also why Claude was unaffected: it defaults to `true` and has no experiment, so the experiment-blind process registers it from the default.

## Fix

Forward the renderer's experiment-aware value to the agent host over the AHP root channel (`root/configChanged`), reusing the same mechanism already used for telemetry level, session sync, and terminal auto-approve. The host registers Codex when it sees the value enabled (in addition to the existing env-var fast path), reacting via `onDidRootConfigChange`.

- **Schema** (`agentHostSchema.ts`): new root-config key `codexAgentEnabled` on `platformRootSchema`.
- **Renderers** (`localAgentHostService.ts` + `remoteAgentHostProtocolClient.ts`): push the value on connect and on setting change.
- **Host** (`agentHostMain.ts`): register Codex on enable via `onDidRootConfigChange`, idempotently, keeping the SDK-availability gate.

Works identically for the desktop (utility process) and remote (server) topologies, since both renderer clients push over the same channel.

## Behavior

- **Enabling** (via experiment or setting) now registers Codex provider live, but agent host restart still needed to fetch models.
- **Disabling** still takes effect on the next agent host restart. Registration is intentionally one-way (register-on-enable): live unregister would require tearing down in-progress Codex sessions and per-client refcounting across windows, which is out of scope here.

## Testing

- Added a unit test asserting the connect flow forwards `codexAgentEnabled` (and a dedicated test for the `true` case).
- Verified end-to-end on a local Code OSS dev build: with the agent host spawned with `VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_CODEX_AGENT_ENABLED=false` (simulating the experiment-blind process), the renderer's `root/configChanged` push alone caused `Registering agent provider: codex`, and Codex appeared in the root-state agents list. Confirmed via the AHP wire log and `agenthost.log`.

title: agentHost: aggregate multi-chat progress and changes to the session
body:
Fixes #322418

## Problem
Local agent host sessions that contain multiple (peer) chats did not surface sub-chat **progress** or **file changes** at the session level:

1. The session status stayed `Idle` while a peer chat was actively working, and individual chat tabs didn't show progress.
2. The session header **Changes** pill never appeared in multi-chat sessions, so there was no way to open the aggregated changes view.

## Changes

### Progress aggregation (host-side)
- `_aggregateChatSummaries` now promotes the aggregated session status to `InProgress` when **any** chat is running.
- The host forwards each chat's own status to the session catalog (`SessionChatUpdated`) so every chat tab — not just the first — shows progress.
- The default tab reflects its own status via a `_defaultChatStatusOverride` in the provider.

### Changes aggregation (host-side)
Each peer chat records its file edits into its **own** database (the chat URI is used as the session URI for that chat's edit tracker), but the session changeset previously only read the session DB — so peer-chat edits were invisible at the session level.

- New `computeUnionedDiffs(sources, diffService)` in `sessionDiffAggregator.ts` unions the session DB with every peer chat DB. Each file identity tracks which source owns its first/last snapshot, so the `session-db:` content URIs encode the correct database and resolve to the right blobs.
- `computeSessionDiffs` full-mode now delegates to `computeUnionedDiffs` (single-source case), keeping the single-chat incremental fast/slow paths intact.
- `agentHostChangesetService`'s edit-tracker fallback opens the peer chat DBs and unions them (disposed in `finally`); the git fast-path now keys off the **latest turn across all chats** (the shared working tree's most recent checkpoint) instead of only the default chat's last turn.

## Notes for reviewers
- **Single-chat sessions are byte-for-byte unchanged** — `_openPeerChatSources` returns empty and the existing incremental path is used; `_latestTurnIdAcrossChats` short-circuits to the previous one-liner.
- **No impact on session open** — opening/restoring a session only reads persisted summaries; the new code runs only on compute triggers (turn complete / opening the changes view).
- The multi-chat union always does a **full** recompute (it skips the incremental optimization). This is a deliberate correctness-over-micro-optimization tradeoff and is documented as a follow-up debt item with `TODO` markers in `sessionDiffAggregator.ts` and `agentHostChangesetService.ts`.

## Tests
- New `computeUnionedDiffs` unit tests (multi-source union, per-source content-URI encoding, cross-source before/after).
- New multi-chat status aggregation/forwarding tests.
- All existing `computeSessionDiffs`/`computeTurnDiffs` (16) and `AgentHostStateManager` (54) tests pass. typecheck + hygiene + eslint clean.

title: sessions: surface un-accepted PR review comments to the agent
body:
Fixes #322172

## Problem  When working with agent feedback in an agent-host session, un-accepted **PR review comments** were invisible to the agent. The agent-host `listComments` tool appends a note ("there are N pull request comments which the user has not reviewed yet") and the `viewUnreviewedComments` tool reveals those comments — but both read **only** agent-feedback annotations whose `_meta` is `kind: 'prReview'` + `state: 'created'`.  Un-accepted PR review comments lived only client-side in `CodeReviewService` (`prReviewState`, keyed by session resource) and were never written to the session's annotations channel. So the note always said zero and `viewUnreviewedComments` returned nothing. (The channel-key resolution itself is fine: the server already normalizes peer-chat URIs to the owning session, and the client resolves the channel via `session.sessionId`, so a session's comments stay on one channel across multiple chats.)  ## Fix  Add `AgentFeedbackPRReviewSeederContribution`, which mirrors the active agent-host session's un-accepted PR review comments onto the feedback annotations channel as `created` `prReview` items, **keyed by the session resource** (the same key every other feedback op uses). Each mirror carries `sourcePRReviewCommentId` so it can be de-duplicated against the raw PR comment in the editor and so resolving it resolves the originating GitHub thread.  The seeder is idempotent and self-healing: - seeds a `created` mirror for each PR comment that has none; - refreshes a `created` mirror's text when the upstream comment body changes; - collapses duplicate `created` mirrors for the same source (benign echo race / two windows); - removes a `created` mirror when its source PR comment disappears (resolved upstream, converted, or dismissed), while keeping accepted/submitted mirrors.  Supporting changes: - `IAgentFeedbackItemsBackend.hasLoaded` / `IAgentFeedbackService.hasLoadedFeedback` (+ a one-time "snapshot loaded" event) so the seeder waits for the authoritative annotations snapshot before acting — avoiding duplicate mirrors on reload. - `ICodeReviewService.dismissPRReviewComment`: deleting a comment from the `viewUnreviewedComments` confirmation now suppresses the source PR comment so the seeder does not immediately recreate the mirror. - `getSessionEditorComments` de-duplicates the two representations in the editor: a still-`created` mirror is hidden (raw PR comment shown with its native actions); once accepted/submitted the mirror supersedes the raw comment.  ## Notes for reviewers  - Only the **active** session is seeded by design — `CodeReviewService` only loads PR review threads for the active session, and mirrors persist as server-side annotations so they survive a session going inactive. This is documented in the seeder. - A rubber-duck review was run; findings (stale mirror content, non-sticky delete, active-session rationale) were addressed, plus a self-healing duplicate-collapse for the snapshot-echo race. - Tests added: seeder behavior (`agentFeedbackPRReviewSeeder.test.ts`), editor de-dup (`sessionEditorComments.test.ts`), and `dismissPRReviewComment` (`codeReviewService.test.ts`). - :warning: Hygiene/compile and the test suites could not be executed in the authoring environment (no `node_modules`/build tooling). All changed files pass language-server diagnostics; please run the agentFeedback/codeReview unit tests in CI/locally before merging. title: Fix Open Host Settings command from the command palette
body:
Follow-up to #323044.

The "Open Host Settings" command only worked from the session context menu, which passes a session argument. When invoked from the Command Palette there was no argument, so `run` returned early and did nothing.

This PR:
- Falls back to the active session (`ISessionsService.activeSession`) when no context is passed, so the palette invocation opens host settings for the active session.
- Gates the command on the active session being an agent host provider via a `precondition`, so it is only enabled in the palette when relevant.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Fix single tool calls getting stuck inside thinking parts
body:
## Problem

When a thinking/"Working" section contains exactly one tool call (and no reasoning text), that tool should be promoted to the top level instead of staying nested inside the collapsed thinking part. In several cases it stayed stuck:

1. **Multi-child tools** — the promotion bailed out whenever the tool's rendered DOM had more than one child element, so terminal/search/edit tools (command + output, etc.) never got promoted.
2. **Late completion** — `finalizeTitleIfDefault()` is one-shot, so if the tool hadn't reported `Completed`/`Cancelled` at that exact instant, promotion was skipped and never retried.
3. **Lost original position** — `singleItemInfo` (which records where to move the tool back to) gets wiped whenever the item count isn't 1, so a transient sibling item or eager rendering left us with `undefined` and nothing to promote.

## Fix

- Removed the `childElementCount > 1` guard so a lone tool is promoted regardless of tool type.
- When the tool isn't complete yet at finalize, observe its state and promote it once it completes (instead of giving up permanently).
- Persist each tool's original position (`toolOriginalPositionByCallId`) so a lone tool can always be reconstructed and promoted, even after a sibling came and went.

Net result: a single tool call is reliably promoted to the top level regardless of its type, DOM shape, or completion timing.

Adds regression tests covering all three cases.

title: fix: guard against missing default agent in chat sendRequest (fixes #321962)
body:
### Summary

`ChatService.sendRequest` crashes downstream consumers with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'metadata')` because it asserts the result of `getDefaultAgent(...)` with a non-null assertion (`!`). `getDefaultAgent` is declared `IChatAgent | undefined` and legitimately returns `undefined` when no activated default agent matches the request **location and mode**. The asserted `undefined` is then assigned to `data.agent` — declared non-nullable (`IChatAgentData`) — and fired through `onDidSubmitAgent`, where the consumer `repopulateAgentCommand` dereferences `agent.metadata.isSticky` and throws.

The fix removes the non-null assertion at the producer and rejects the request when no default agent exists, mirroring the guard already present on the queued-request path.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#321962
and fixes #321961
Recommended reviewer: `@roblourens`

### Culprit Commit

A single culprit commit could not be definitively isolated from the available shallow checkout (no history for `git blame`/`git log` ranges). The defect itself is the **long-standing non-null assertion** at `chatServiceImpl.ts:1018` (`getDefaultAgent(...)!`), which lies to the type system about a value that the method's own signature declares can be `undefined`.

The latent producer bug became observable once the crash-site consumer began dereferencing `agent.metadata` directly: `repopulateAgentCommand` in `chatInputEditorContrib.ts` (handler wired to `onDidSubmitAgent`) reads `agent.metadata.isSticky` with no nullability check. The producer `!` and an identical one in `resendRequest` (line 892) both predate and are independent of that consumer change — the type-system bypass is the root cause, not the consumer.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant W as ChatWidget
    participant S as ChatService
    participant A as ChatAgentService
    participant C as InputContrib

    U->>W: submit input (no `@agent` part)
    W->>S: sendRequest(location, mode)
    S->>A: getDefaultAgent(location, mode)
    A-->>S: undefined (no default agent for this location+mode)
    Note over S: line 1018: getDefaultAgent(...)! asserts non-undefined (BYPASS)
    S-->>W: data.agent = undefined (contract says IChatAgentData)
    W->>C: onDidSubmitAgent({ agent: undefined })
    Note over C: repopulateAgentCommand reads agent.metadata.isSticky
    C-->>C: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'metadata')
```

### Affected Files

| File | Role | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts` | **Producer / bypass (fixed)** | Line 1018 `getDefaultAgent(location, options?.modeInfo?.kind)!` — the `!` lets `undefined` flow into `agent` (1026) and `data.agent` (1035). |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/participants/chatAgents.ts` | Why the value is undefined | `getDefaultAgent(...): IChatAgent \| undefined` (interface line 270, impl line 442) returns `undefined` when no activated default agent matches the location+mode. |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatService.ts` | Violated contract | `IChatSendRequestData.agent: IChatAgentData` is non-nullable. |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts` | Event boundary | Line 2704 fires `onDidSubmitAgent({ agent: sent.data.agent, ... })`; line 2687 already early-returns on `ChatSendResult.isRejected(result)`. |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/editor/chatInputEditorContrib.ts` | Crash site (not modified) | Line 454 `} else if (agent.metadata.isSticky) {` in `repopulateAgentCommand`. |

### Repro Steps

1. Open a chat surface in a location + mode combination for which no activated agent is registered as the default (e.g. a mode whose default participant has not finished activating, or a location with no matching `isDefault` agent).
2. Submit a request that contains **no** explicit `@agent` part and for which no silent agent is configured.
3. `getDefaultAgent` returns `undefined`; the non-null assertion passes it through to `data.agent`; `onDidSubmitAgent` fires with `agent: undefined`; `repopulateAgentCommand` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'metadata')`.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts` (line 1018):

Removed the non-null assertion on `getDefaultAgent` and added a guard that warns and returns a rejected result when no default agent is available:

```ts
const defaultAgent = this.chatAgentService.getDefaultAgent(location, options?.modeInfo?.kind);
if (!defaultAgent) {
    this.logService.warn('sendRequest', `No default agent for location ${location}`);
    return { kind: 'rejected', reason: 'No default agent available' };
}
```

This fixes the bug **at the data producer**, where the invalid `undefined` first enters `data.agent` — not at the crash site, and not by making the event/contract nullable (which would push undefined-handling onto every consumer). After this change, `agent` at line 1026 and `data.agent` at line 1035 are provably non-undefined because the guard narrows `defaultAgent` to `IChatAgentData` before either is computed.

The reject path is already a designed, graceful outcome: `chatWidget._acceptInput` checks `ChatSendResult.isRejected(result)` and returns early, so no agent submission fires and `repopulateAgentCommand` is never reached. The guard intentionally **mirrors the identical guard already present on the queued-request path** (`processNextPendingRequest`), which uses the same `logService.warn` + `{ kind: 'rejected', reason: 'No default agent available' }` shape — strong evidence this is the intended pattern and that the non-queued path was an inconsistency.

**Related observation (not changed):** `resendRequest` (line 892) contains the same `getDefaultAgent(...)!` assertion, but it returns `Promise<void>` and never constructs `data.agent` or fires `onDidSubmitAgent`, so it is not the producer for this crash. Left unchanged to keep the fix surgical; flagging it for the owner as a separate hardening opportunity.

**Alternatives considered:**
- Guard at the crash site in `chatInputEditorContrib.ts` — rejected: hides the symptom while `undefined` still flows through the non-nullable `data.agent` contract to every other consumer.
- Make `onDidSubmitAgent` / `IChatSendRequestData.agent` nullable — rejected: spreads undefined-handling across all consumers instead of preventing the invalid value at its single producer.

### Recommended Owner

**`@roblourens`** — per the engineering working-areas registry, he owns the **Chat participant API** and **ChatModel creation, management, persistence** in `vscode`, which is exactly the `ChatService.sendRequest` request-flow and `getDefaultAgent` participant-resolution code touched here. He is a core maintainer with write access and is highly active across the chat area. (Team-membership and liveness verification via the GitHub API could not be executed in this environment, but his ownership of this area is well established.)

title: Claude agent host: native (BYOK) transport (Phases 18–19)
body: ## What Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/314952 Adds **native (BYOK) access** for the Claude agent host and the **transport-branched model source** it builds on (roadmap Phases 18 & 19). When `claudeUseCopilotProxy: false`, the Claude Agent SDK uses whatever Claude is configured with **directly** on the user's own credentials — no Copilot proxy in the request path. Proxy mode (the default) is unchanged. ## How to use This is only through the Agent Host, so first apply these VS Code settings: ``` "chat.agentHost.enabled": true, "chat.editor.claude.preferAgentHost": true, "chat.agents.claude.preferAgentHost": true ``` Then, we need to apply _Agent Host Settings_ so right click on an _agent host_ session in the Agents Window: Choose "Open Host Settings" and then add `claudeUseCopilotProxy: false` to that. ## Highlights - **Phase 18 — transport-branched model source.** Proxy mode lists Claude models from CAPI; native mode enumerates via the SDK's `query().supportedModels()`. Single branch point (`_refreshModels` → proxy/native). - **Phase 19 — direct Claude access.** Native transport omits the proxy base-url/auth-token and lets the SDK resolve credentials itself. - **Native auth = subprocess env.** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or a subscription OAuth token in `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (from `claude setup-token`). Fixes SDK ≥0.3 **env-replace** semantics by spreading `process.env` in native mode so the token + `PATH` actually reach the `claude` subprocess (previously wiped → "Not logged in"). - **`IClaudeAgentSdkService` stays 1:1 with the SDK.** Adds a `query()` passthrough; the model-enumeration orchestration moved to the caller, which `close()`s the throwaway query (leak guard, covered by a test). - **Cleanup:** removed the speculative native-binary-path feature (it only selects which `claude` build runs, never the credentials); moved `ClaudeTransport` into `claudeProxyService.ts`; dropped a trivial model-list helper; simplified `buildSubprocessEnv`. > Note: the interactive `claude login` keychain session is **not** used in headless/SDK mode — verified empirically. Headless subscription auth requires `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. ## Test plan - `./scripts/test.sh --grep "claude|Claude"` — all green (incl. native env-inheritance, native model enumeration, and the new close()/leak-guard test). - `npm run typecheck-client` — clean. - E2E: launched Code OSS `--agents` with `claudeUseCopilotProxy: false` + `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; native turns authenticate and the model picker shows native models with no proxy started. Draft — opening for early review.

🎥  below -- adds a UI toggle for sandboxing for the local harness in the picker and also clarifies in the label of the mode that sandboxing is on. This whole thing is off by default and we can turn it on via an experiment. 

I will try to further tweak tomorrow how things look, especially the `Default Approvals (Sandboxed)` part which looks pretty ugly. Ideas welcome!

---

🤖 

## Overview

Adds an inline **"Sandboxing for terminal"** toggle to the **Default Approvals** option of the permissions picker. Instead of two separate Default Approvals rows (plain vs. sandboxed), there is now a single Default Approvals option with the sandbox switch contained inside it.

## Permissions picker changes

- The Default Approvals option hosts an inline pill switch ("Sandboxing for terminal") on its own row, in both the open dropdown and reflected on the closed trigger button (which reads "Default Approvals (Sandboxed)" when sandboxing is on).
- The toggle reflects and updates **`chat.agent.sandbox.enabled`** (`on` / `off`).
- Clicking the toggle flips sandboxing without selecting/closing the row; clicking the row still selects Default Approvals as before.
- Enterprise policy gating, the "Learn more about permissions" footer, and the existing Bypass/Autopilot levels are unchanged.

## Gating

- The whole sandbox-toggle UI is behind a new experimental setting **`chat.experimental.permissionsSandboxToggle.enabled`** (off by default), since it is a significant UI change.
- The toggle is shown **only for the Local harness**. Agent-host harnesses (Copilot CLI, Claude Code, Codex, …) opt out via the picker delegate and never show it.

## New reusable action-list primitive

- Adds a generic `inlineToggle` capability to the action-widget list items (`actionList` / `actionWidgetDropdown`): an item can host an always-visible pill switch on its own row, with appropriate item height, click-to-select exclusion, and an accessible label that announces the switch state.
- Adds the supporting CSS for the iOS-style pill switch (themed, with high-contrast support) and a `className` passthrough on dropdown actions.

## Tests / fixtures

- New `permissionPickerList` component fixture covering the three states: toggle hidden, shown + off, shown + on.
- `chatInput` gains a `WithSandboxing` variant that renders the local harness in the sandboxed state; fixture service mocks were extended to support it.

## Follow-ups

- Removing the `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled: "network"` value is intentionally left for a separate PR.

title: Background todo agent reliability fixes
body:
1. Prompt hard invariants (backgroundTodoPrompt.tsx)

Adds an explicit "Hard invariants" block to both system messages (main loop and final-review) that the model must never violate:
  - Completed items are never dropped — every item that exists in the current list must appear in the output.
  - IDs and titles are preserved across updates unless scope genuinely changed.
  - Status is monotonically forward-progressing; a completed item cannot regress.
  - Exactly one item must be in-progress whenever any unfinished item exists.
  - Completed items appear before unfinished items; out-of-order completions are handled by reordering, not renumbering.
  - Also removes the old "Sequential state rules" block, which required work to proceed in strict list order — conflicting with real agent behaviour where later items are often completed first.

2. Final-review recovery (backgroundTodoProcessor.ts)

requestFinalReview() was a no-op whenever the current processor instance hadn't created any todos itself (_hasCreatedTodos = false). After a reload or when a fresh processor picks up an existing chat, the list was never finalized at the end of a turn.

Fix: when _hasCreatedTodos is false, the processor now asynchronously probes the todo provider. If a non-empty list is found in the session, the finalize pass runs normally; otherwise it skips as before. The probe is fire-and-forget so it cannot block the main agent turn.
